Suppose we have the matrix of demeaned data points $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \amp 1 \amp -3 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp -3 \\ \end{bmatrix}$ that we considered in [preview-quadforms]. The data points are shown in [fig-covariance-quad].

The set of demeaned data points from [preview-quadforms].

Constructing the covariance matrix $C=\frac13~AA^T$ gives $C=\begin{bmatrix} 14/3 \amp 13/3 \\ 13/3 \amp 14/3 \end{bmatrix}$, which has eigenvalues $\lambda_1 = 9$, with associated eigenvector $\twovec{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/\sqrt{2}}$, and $\lambda_2=1/3$, with associated eigenvector $\twovec{-1/\sqrt{2}}{1/\sqrt{2}}$.

Remember that the variance in a direction $\uvec$ is $ V_{\uvec} = \uvec\cdot(C\uvec) = q_C(\uvec)$. Therefore, the variance attains a maximum value of 9 in the direction $\twovec{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/\sqrt{2}}$ and a minimum value of 1/3 in the direction $\twovec{-1/\sqrt{2}}{1/\sqrt{2}}$. [fig-quad-project] shows the data projected onto the lines defined by these vectors.

The demeaned data from [preview-quadforms] is shown projected onto the lines of maximal and minimal variance.

Remember that variance is additive, as stated in [prop-variance-additivity], which tells us that the total variance is $V = 9 + 1/3 = 28/3$.
